Massachusetts: what's on the November 3, 2026 ballot

Every candidate below is listed alphabetically, with party shown as text only. Open a name for their stated positions, background and recent news, each with sources.

Open Massachusetts on the map

Key dates

  • Early in-person voting: October 17, 2026 to October 30, 2026. Dates, hours and locations vary by city or town. Check the Secretary of the Commonwealth's early voting lookup.
  • Voter registration deadline (online, by mail, or in person): October 24, 2026. Registration forms sent by mail must be postmarked by this date.
  • Deadline to apply for a vote-by-mail ballot: October 27, 2026. Applications must be received by 5 p.m. You can request an absentee ballot in person until November 2.
  • Election Day: November 3, 2026. Polls are open from 7 a.m. to 8 p.m.

Official election information: vote.gov

Who's running

Only the U.S. Senate and governor races are loaded so far. Other statewide offices, ballot measures, U.S. House and local races aren't loaded yet. Check your sample ballot for the full list.

Federal

Senator in Congress

This election fills one six-year term in the U.S. Senate, and incumbent Democrat Edward J. Markey is running for re-election.

State

Governor & Lieutenant Governor

Governor and lieutenant governor are elected together for a four-year term, and incumbent Governor Maura Healey is running for re-election. The tickets are Healey with Kim Driscoll (Democratic), Minogue with Shawn Oliver (Republican), and James with Kayla Kittredge (Independent).

Republican running mate Shawn Oliver has suspended his campaign, but he is still on the ballot.
